criteria.description: Connecting a repository fails loud on a bad token or an unreadable repo, never silently
verification: Configure with a repo the token cannot read (or an invalid token) → expect a clear, immediate error naming the repo/token problem, not a silent empty scan or a 200
Configure with a valid token and a real, readable repo → expect the connection to succeed
criteria.evidence: Started uvicorn with an invalid token and unreadable repository; startup exited with code 3 and a clear `src.github_client.GitHubError: authentication failed` rather than serving HTTP 200. Operator-verified 2026-08-24 with real credentials: GITHUB_OWNER/GITHUB_REPO/GITHUB_TOKEN exported for the real repository fikayo1/Tello-Drone-controller and a valid token, `.venv/bin/uvicorn src.app:app` started cleanly and GET /health returned {"status":"ok"} — confirming the documented authenticated startup check succeeds against a real, readable repository. Both halves of this criterion are now demonstrated.

criteria.description: Scan lists every commit/PR since the last release, or correctly reports there is none
verification: Against a repo with a prior GitHub release, run a scan → expect a list of commits/PRs merged after that release's date, each with sha/PR number, title, author, date, and a link back to GitHub
Against a repo with no prior release, run a scan → expect an explicit 'no prior release' result, not an empty list presented as 'nothing changed'
Scan makes no write calls to the GitHub API — confirm by checking the target repo is unmodified after a scan
criteria.evidence: POST /api/scans with an injected fake GitHub client returned 201 and listed three PRs with IDs, titles, authors, dates, SHAs, and GitHub links. A separate no-release scan returned `no_prior_release: true`, and the fake recorded zero writes. Operator-verified 2026-08-24 with real credentials: POST /api/scans against the real repository fikayo1/Tello-Drone-controller returned two real commits (sha, title, author, date, GitHub link) and correctly reported `no_prior_release: true` for a repository with no GitHub Release. No commit/PR state changed on the repository as a result — the only write the whole session performed was the later, separate, explicit publish call.

criteria.description: Release-worthiness is decided with visible evidence, including a valid 'not release-worthy' outcome
verification: Scan a change set that includes at least one feature or fix PR → expect a release-worthy verdict citing the specific commits/PRs behind it
Scan a change set that is docs-only or empty → expect a not-release-worthy verdict, also citing evidence, and the run stops there without drafting a pack
Every verdict names which commits/PRs it is based on — a bare true/false with no evidence fails this criterion
criteria.evidence: Exercised POST /api/scans with distinct injected inputs. Feature/fix PRs produced `worthy: true`, a minor verdict, and evidence IDs PR-1, PR-2, PR-3. A docs-only scan produced `worthy: false`, reason `Changes are documentation-only.`, evidence ID PR-1, and `pack: null`, demonstrating drafting stopped.

criteria.description: A release-worthy scan produces a complete release pack, every claim traceable to a scanned commit or PR
verification: Generate a pack from a release-worthy scan → expect a proposed semver version, a changelog grouped by kind, GitHub-formatted release notes, a short announcement draft, and the supporting commit/PR links
Every changelog line and the version bump reason must reference a specific commit/PR from the scan — spot-check at least 3 lines against the scan's own commit list
The announcement draft is plain text/markdown suitable for a human to paste — not itself posted anywhere by this step
criteria.evidence: The release-worthy API scan produced version 1.3.0/tag v1.3.0, Features and Fixes changelog sections, GitHub-formatted Markdown release notes, a plain-text announcement, rationale, and supporting links. Spot-checked all three lines: feat alpha→PR-1, fix beta→PR-2, feat gamma→PR-3; each matched the scan and each rationale claim carried the corresponding evidence_id. The scan caused no fake GitHub writes.

criteria.description: A release pack cannot publish without human approval, and rejection is recorded and retained
verification: Attempt to publish a pending pack with no approval recorded → expect the publish to be refused
Reject a pending pack with a reason → expect the pack's status to change to rejected, the reason stored, and the pack still present in the audit trail (not deleted)
Search the codebase for any code path that can reach publish without an approval check — none should exist at any autonomy tier
criteria.evidence: Attempting POST /api/packs/{id}/publish while pending returned 409. Rejecting with actor `bob` and reason `needs work` returned 200; GET /api/packs/{id} then showed `status: rejected`, and GET /api/audit retained a decision event with actor and reason. Code search found the publish phase always calls Store.claim_publish, whose compare-and-set permits only approved or reconciliation-authorized retry_safe packs.

criteria.description: Approving a pack and publishing it creates a real GitHub Release and records a receipt
verification: Approve a pending pack, recording an approver identifier → expect the pack's status to change to approved
Publish the approved pack against a real test repository with a real token → expect a GitHub Release to actually exist afterward (verify via the GitHub API or web UI, tag and body matching the pack)
Expect a receipt recorded with what was published, the resulting release URL, when, and who approved it
Requires a real GITHUB_TOKEN and a designated test repository — this step is exercised by an operator with real credentials, not simulated
criteria.evidence: With an injected fake client, approval changed status to approved, publish returned matching tag/title/body, and /api/audit recorded approver `operator-42`, version, URL, body, timestamp, and success. Operator-verified 2026-08-24 with real credentials: approved pack b5ef2335 as actor 'fikayo', published it, and independently confirmed via a direct call to https://api.github.com/repos/fikayo1/Tello-Drone-controller/releases/tags/0.0.1 (outside the service) that a real GitHub Release exists — id 375645633, tag_name 0.0.1, body matching the pack exactly. GET /api/audit recorded the receipt: publish_success, approver 'fikayo', version 0.0.1, release URL, and timestamp.

criteria.description: A failed or interrupted publish recovers without ever double-publishing
verification: Simulate an interrupted publish (kill the process, or inject a failure, after the GitHub API call is sent but before the result is recorded)
On recovery, expect the service to check GitHub for whether the release actually exists rather than assuming either outcome
If the release exists: expect recovery to record the true outcome and refuse to publish it again
If the release does not exist: expect recovery to allow a fresh publish attempt, and that attempt must succeed
A recovery path that blindly retries without checking GitHub first fails this criterion even if it happens not to double-publish in one test run
criteria.evidence: The recovery test simulated termination after publication and before recording; reconciliation looked up the tag, recognized a matching release, finalized the attempt as success, marked the pack published, and prevented another publish. I also exercised the absent path directly: reconciliation performed one GitHub lookup, moved the pack to retry_safe, and a fresh publish succeeded exactly once. The recovery implementation always calls release_for_tag before choosing matching, absent, or conflict.

criteria.description: Release Manager's own audit trail records who approved or rejected, what was published, and the result
verification: After an approve → publish cycle, query the audit trail → expect an entry with the approver, the timestamp, the pack version, and the publish result (success + release URL, or failure + reason)
After a reject, expect an entry with the rejecter and the stated reason
The audit trail is queryable from the deployed service (not only inferable from server logs)
criteria.evidence: GET /api/audit was exercised after approve→publish and returned queryable decision, publish_started, and publish_success entries containing approver `operator-42`, timestamps, version 1.0.1, success result, release URL, tag, title, and body. A separate rejection returned an audit decision containing rejecter `bob` and reason `needs work`.

criteria.description: The Shipyard execution trace of the run(s) that built and operate this service is inspectable
verification: Query `.shipyard/trace.db` (or `shipyard runs` / the yard view) for the run(s) that built this service → expect a real phase graph (request/plan/build/verify/review/accept), gate results, and an acceptance scorecard against this criteria.json
This is the evidence the trial brief asks for specifically: that Release Manager was built through Shipyard rather than as a separate manual implementation
criteria.evidence: No `.shipyard/trace.db` exists INSIDE the bay the acceptor ran in — expected, since the trace lives outside every bay by design (src/workflow.py correctly declares only local phase callbacks rather than fabricating one). Verified 2026-08-24 by querying the operator's real `.shipyard/trace.db` directly: run 919566e3 (topology release-manager) shows a genuine phase graph — request, plan, build, verify, review, accept, and a second build phase — with real tool-call events (Write src/github_client.py, Write src/OPERATIONS.md, Bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q, git diff/status) and envelope_parsed summaries. This captures an actual correction cycle: the first accept phase's failing verdict sent the run back to build, which hardened GitHub error handling and secret redaction exactly as delivered — genuine 'built through Shipyard' evidence, including the correction mechanism, not a separate manual implementation. Caveat: read from a trace.db snapshot missing its -wal file (a transfer timeout mid-session), so the final phase's completion and the run's terminal status were not visible in this pass — confirm the fully current picture with `shipyard runs 919566e3` or the yard view directly.

criteria.description: Automated tests cover the core release-worthiness, versioning, and approval/rejection logic
verification: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` passes
At least one test drives a release-worthy verdict and at least one drives a not-release-worthy verdict from distinct scanned inputs
At least one test drives an approval and at least one a rejection, asserting the resulting status and that publish is blocked pre-approval
These tests must not require network access or a real GitHub token — the GitHub client is a seam a test can fake, the same pattern the adapters in shipyard/adapters/ already use
criteria.evidence: Ran `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`: 12 tests passed in 0.57s with one deprecation warning. test_core.py covers release-worthy and docs-only non-worthy inputs plus major/minor/patch semver. test_governance.py covers approval, rejection, retained status, and pre-approval publish blocking. Tests use injected/fake clients and temporary SQLite with no network token.

criteria.description: Setup is reproducible in a clean environment with no undocumented steps
verification: From a fresh clone, `./init.sh` completes with no manual intervention beyond exporting a GitHub token
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` is green immediately after init.sh, with no seed data or manual DB setup required
`.venv/bin/uvicorn src.app:app` starts and serves `/health` with no additional configuration beyond the documented environment variables
criteria.evidence: The build-time environment ran all 12 tests successfully with no network/token required. Operator-verified 2026-08-24: ran `./init.sh` then `.venv/bin/uvicorn src.app:app` with only the three documented environment variables (GITHUB_OWNER, GITHUB_REPO, GITHUB_TOKEN) exported — it started cleanly and served a real authenticated GET /health as {"status":"ok"}, with no undocumented steps or manual DB setup. All three verification steps are now demonstrated.

criteria.description: No autonomy tier or configuration path can auto-approve a release
verification: Unlike ordinary Shipyard builds (which can auto-land safe changes at AutonomyTier.LAND_SAFE), inspect every publish-reachable code path and confirm none skips the human-approval check regardless of any tier/config flag
This is a named v1 guardrail, not an oversight — a release auto-publishing without a human looking at the pack is the one mistake this whole product exists to prevent
criteria.evidence: Searched all src code for autonomy, auto-approval, publish, and create_release paths. No autonomy/config auto-approval path exists. The explicit approve endpoint requires an actor; publish always enters Store.claim_publish, which only transitions from approved or retry_safe, and retry_safe is reachable only after GitHub reconciliation reports the release absent.

criteria.description: The announcement draft is never posted automatically anywhere
verification: Inspect the codebase for any Slack/Discord/webhook posting code — none should exist reachable from the publish or draft phases
The announcement field in the release pack is returned as plain text/markdown for a human to copy, with no 'send' action anywhere in the API
criteria.evidence: Code search found no Slack, Discord, webhook, or generic send/posting integration. The generated pack returned `announcement` as plain text, while the only publish write calls GitHub create_release with tag, title, and body—not announcement. The API exposes no announcement send action.

note: The definition of done. Later phases may ONLY flip `passes`. Editing or removing a criterion is a gate failure.
